name: Tech-Lead Execute B — loop_engine task tree decomposition
description: Version B: to-tickets initial decomposition → loop_engine convergence (break tasks down until atomic) → kanban_chains dispatch. Same verify/fix/close as A.

nodes.body_template:
## Task-Tree Decomposition (loop_engine convergence)

**Spec card:** ${trigger.card_id}
**Title:** ${trigger.title}

You are the tech-lead. The PO wrote the spec — DO NOT grill the user.

### Phase 1: Initial Decomposition

Read the spec. Load your `to-tickets` skill. Produce an initial task list — coarse-grained is fine. Each task needs: title, acceptance criteria, dependencies.

### Phase 2: Converge with loop_engine (CRITICAL)

Call `loop_engine` to iterate on decomposition quality. This is NOT code execution — it's task analysis.

Configure loop_engine with these phases:
- **Execution phase** (assignee: tech-lead): Review each task. If a task is too big for a junior dev to complete in one sitting, break it into 2-3 sub-tasks. If a task has multiple independent concerns, split them. Update the task list.
- **Verifier phase** (assignee: verifier): Check each task for atomicity. A task is atomic when: (a) a junior dev can complete it in one sitting, (b) it has clear testable acceptance criteria, (c) it can be verified independently, (d) it's not two tasks disguised as one. Output: advance (all atomic), replan (some still too big), escalate (spec ambiguous).

Set max_iterations to 5. The loop converges when the verifier says all tasks are atomic.

### Phase 3: Dispatch via kanban_chains

When converged, you have a task tree. Only dispatch LEAF tasks (the atomic ones). Call `kanban_chains`:
- One chain per leaf task (or sequential steps in one chain for dependent tasks)
- Each chain step: {assignee: "developer", title: "[task] <title>", body: "<acceptance criteria>"}
- Your card auto-blocks. Do NOT call kanban_complete.

After auto-promotion: read verifier summaries. Complete with plan metadata.

**Completion metadata:**
```
{plan_complete: true, task_count: N, task_ids: ["t_xxx", ...], decomposition_iterations: N, sizing_summary: "small:N medium:N large:N"}
```

## Adversarial Behavior Verification

**Spec card:** ${trigger.card_id}
**Tasks completed:** ${nodes.plan.output.task_count}

Your goal: TRY TO BREAK the integrated code. Prove the developer's claims are true by EXECUTING behavior tests — not by reading code.

### Phase 1: Spec → Behavior Test Matrix

Read the spec. Extract EVERY requirement. For each, write a BEHAVIOR test that proves it works through the PUBLIC INTERFACE:
- CLI tools: pipe input, check stdout/stderr/exit code
- REST APIs: HTTP requests, check status codes + response bodies
- Libraries: import and call public functions, check return values

Do NOT test implementation details. Test BEHAVIOR — what the user sees. These tests must survive refactors.

Write all behavior tests to a file (e.g. test_behavior.py). These tests are YOUR weapon.

### Phase 2: Execute — Break It

Run ALL tests: developer's existing tests AND your new behavior tests. Any failure is a finding.

Try inputs the developer didn't anticipate: empty input, huge input, special characters, Unicode, boundary values, production-mode testing, error paths.

### Phase 3: Do NOT Edit Dev Code

You must NOT modify the developer's code. You only write tests AGAINST it.

**Verdict:**
- PASS: ALL behavior tests passed.
- FAIL: One or more behavior tests failed.
- ESCALATE: spec is ambiguous or impossible to test.

**Completion metadata:**
```
{verdict: "PASS"|"FAIL"|"ESCALATE", findings_count: N, behavior_tests_total: N, behavior_tests_passed: N, behavior_test_file: "path", production_mode_tested: true}
```

## Re-verify — adversarial behavior testing after fix

**Spec card:** ${trigger.card_id}
**Fix card:** ${nodes.fix.output.findings_fixed} findings fixed

Re-run your behavior tests. Every previously-failing test must now PASS. Then write NEW attack vectors — the fix may have introduced new bugs.

Do NOT edit dev code. Only write tests.

**Completion metadata:**
```
{verdict: "PASS"|"FAIL"|"ESCALATE", findings_count: N, behavior_tests_total: N, behavior_tests_passed: N}
```
